title: Ang 1172–1185: the Gurus in Basant
hookLine: spring hymns of the third, fourth and fifth Gurus
tomorrow: the headings jump from five to nine. where did six to eight go?

lines: A HOSPITAL PARKING LOT IN APRIL.
cards: A hospital parking lot in April. The trees along the curb are in full bloom, pink and white, petals on the windshields. A man walks out through the sliding doors after a hard conversation with a doctor, and stops.
Everything is blooming. Birds are loud. Somebody laughs on a bench.
And the thought hits him like a slap: spring is for everybody else. He sits in his car with the petals on the glass and doesn't start the engine. Is he right?
Is spring for some people and not others?

teach.b: Strangely, a Guru agrees with him, and then turns it around. Open to Basant past ang 1172, where the third, fourth and fifth Gurus sing in turn, under the headings Mahala 3, 4 and 5.
Guru Amar Das, the third, sets the scene. In paraphrase: the plants have blossomed, spring has come, and this mind blossoms in the company of the True Guru.

teach.h: TWO SPRINGS: TREES AND A MIND.
teach.b: Two springs, side by side: one in the trees, one in the person. Then on ang 1180, Guru Arjan, the fifth, writes the line that answers the man in the car.
In paraphrase: spring is for the one on whom God is kind. Spring is for the one on whom the Guru has mercy. Always spring, for the one with the Name in the heart.
So yes, spring is only for some. But not the some the man feared. Not the lucky, the healthy, the people laughing on benches.
The Gurus' spring doesn't come with the weather, and so the weather can't take it away.

It comes with kindness received and the Name held close, and that can reach a parked car outside a hospital as easily as a garden. The man starts the engine. Nothing in the hymn makes the news less hard.
It just says a spring is still open to him.

how: Ragis sing the Gurus' Basant hymns in kirtan, Guru Arjan's 'spring is for the one…' refrain among them; readers find each Guru by the headings Mahala 3, 4 and 5.

spring for the one God is kind to

s: in Guru Arjan's Basant hymn, spring is for whoever the season favors
spring is for the one on whom God is kind, with the Name in the heart.
the third Guru's Basant hymn sets blossoming plants beside a blossoming mind
the plants blossom, spring has come, and the mind blossoms in the True Guru's company.
the Basant hymns say hard news should stop hurting when spring comes
they don't make loss smaller; they say a spring stays open even then.

games.q: same week: one friend gets engaged, another gets dumped. the second one texts, "spring for her, winter for me." what does Guru Arjan's Basant line offer?
o: the spring that lasts comes with kindness and the Name, not with good news.
she's right; spring is for whoever got lucky this season.
just wait it out; spring always comes back around next year.
games.why: Guru Arjan: spring is for the one on whom God is kind; always spring for the one with the Name in the heart. it isn't handed out by luck.

practice: For this sit, listen for one living sound: a bird, a voice in another room, your own heartbeat if it's quiet enough. Let it be the spring of this moment, whatever the season is outside.
If you'd like, read ang 1180 before you begin.

wordCard.voice: Ang 1172. Where the Gurus after Guru Nanak take up Basant, and spring turns out to be for anyone with the Name in the heart.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: tis basant, spring is for that one: Guru Arjan's repeated opening on ang 1180.

carryVoice: Spring hymns: the trees bloom on schedule, but the Gurus' spring comes with kindness and the Name. See you tomorrow.
